# Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics — facts

> Source-anchored units about Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics: 13 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.5.1 · generated 2026-11-12 · 13 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] For a Case alert implemented as a Salesforce Flow, activating a new version automatically deactivates the previously active version. An already running Flow interview keeps the version with which it started. This is Flow behavior, not an established contract for an external Pub/Sub alert-rule engine. (high confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_manage.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics · also: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_distribute_activate.htm&language=en_US&type=5, https://salesforce.stackexchange.com/questions/419489/how-to-schedule-a-flow-version-activation
- [statement] Production Flow deployment and activation are separate by default: change sets deploy flows deactivated even when active in the sandbox. Production settings can permit deployment of a new active version through change sets or Metadata API. (high confidence) — https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/flow-implementation-2/deploy-your-flow-to-production · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics · also: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_manage.htm&language=en_US&type=5
- [statement] For native Case escalation rules, activating a rule deactivates existing active escalation rules. Treat this as its own activation mechanism when choosing how to implement Case alerts. (low confidence) — https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/content/learn/modules/service_lex/service_lex_case_manage · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics
- [statement] JSBC Labs warns that reactivating an older Flow version can leave data writes, created records, scheduled actions or external-service effects from the newer version. Its recommendation is a release-level rollback plan that identifies compensation and irreversible external actions. (low confidence) — https://jsbclabs.com/blog/activating-flow-version-is-not-release-management · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics
- [statement] OrgTide describes editing an active Flow as creating a new version while the previously active version keeps running until explicit activation. Its guidance distinguishes saving a change from making that change live. (low confidence) — https://orgtide.com/learn/salesforce-flow-versions · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics
- [statement] Pending scheduled paths of a record-triggered Flow are a distinct case: pending automations use the currently active version when their scheduled time arrives. Do not assume that all deferred Case alerts remain pinned to the version active when queued. (low confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_trigger_scheduled_path.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics
- [statement] Deactivating a record-triggered Flow with scheduled paths does not immediately remove pending rows from the time-based automations list. Salesforce checks activation at their scheduled time and cancels pending automations if the Flow is then deactivated. (low confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_trigger_scheduled_path.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics
- [statement] A new Flow version inherits the existing Flow’s runtime API version; Salesforce releases do not automatically advance that runtime API version. Treat a rule logic revision and a runtime API upgrade as separate changes. (low confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_ref_properties.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics
- [statement] Proposed application policy for an external Case-alert consumer: preserve immutable rule revisions, validate a candidate before activating it, and record an explicit activation boundary. Specify whether queued evaluations retain their assigned revision or resolve the active revision at execution. This is a design recommendation inferred from the different native Flow lifecycles, not a Salesforce Pub/Sub guarantee. (high confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_manage.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics · also: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_trigger_scheduled_path.htm&language=en_US&type=5, https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/flow-implementation-2/deploy-your-flow-to-production

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Before deleting an active Flow version, deactivate it. A Flow with paused interviews cannot be deleted until those interviews finish or are deleted. Retain the versions needed by those interviews during cleanup. (low confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_manage.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics
- [statement] Miguel Diaz initially reported that switching a screen Flow version would fail existing interviews, then corrected that premise in a July 2025 edit. This is a corrected community report, not evidence that activation normally breaks running interviews. (low confidence) — https://salesforce.stackexchange.com/questions/419489/how-to-schedule-a-flow-version-activation · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] JSBC Labs recommends recording the target Flow API name, expected version, activation method, owner and verification window in a release manifest. This is operational advice for making the activated alert logic traceable, rather than a Salesforce-enforced manifest format. (low confidence) — https://jsbclabs.com/blog/activating-flow-version-is-not-release-management · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Proposed activation test policy: exercise both an interview already running and a scheduled path still pending across a version switch. Verify the intended version independently for each lifecycle; a successful test of one does not establish the behavior of the other. (high confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_distribute_activate.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Case alert rule versioning and activation semantics · also: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_trigger_scheduled_path.htm&language=en_US&type=5
